content.title: About
content.content: Fried cod is a member of the cod family prepared by deep‑frying or pan‑frying with a small amount of oil. It has tender white flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and a crispy crust after cooking. The product is commonly served as fillets, patties, or sticks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the most widely caught commercial fish in the North Atlantic and the North Sea.
Cod meat is high in protein and low in fat, making it popular in diet nutrition.
Cod can change the color of its skin depending on the environment, helping it hide from predators.
In Russia, fried cod is often served with mashed potatoes, sauerkraut, or tartar sauce.
Cod can grow over 1.5 m in length, though most catches are 60–80 cm long.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Fried cod provides about 18 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When fried with a modest amount of oil, cod remains relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cod contains vitamin B12, niacin, and vitamin B6, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The fish supplies selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, which support thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than fatty fish, cod still contributes omega‑3s that benefit cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including cod.

items.title: Heavy metal content
items.content: Cod can accumulate small amounts of mercury and other metals; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: High‑calorie frying
items.content: Frying in large amounts of oil significantly increases the dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Foodborne infections
items.content: Undercooked fillet may contain pathogenic bacteria; ensure thorough cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried cod can be served as a standalone dish, in fillet form, as patties, or sticks. It pairs well with lemon, tartar sauce, mayonnaise, fresh vegetables, or a potato side. For a lighter option, use whole‑grain breadcrumbs for the coating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fried cod in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in the freezer for up to 2 months, sealing the package to remove air.
